units.text: This circular informs the industry that the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) will extend the parallel run period of its new online application/submission system for investment products, e-IP, by one month to 29 November 2024. After the extended period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by the Investment Products Division (IPD)1 must be submitted to IPD via e-IP from 30 November 2024.
Background

Following the “Circular on launch of e-IP application/submission system on WINGS” dated 8 July 2024, the SFC launched e-IP on its WINGS2 portal on 29 July 2024 to streamline and enhance the efficiency of processing new product applications and post-authorisation/registration submissions to IPD.

A three-month period of parallel run from the launch of e-IP up to 29 October 2024 was provided at the initial stage. During this period, the SFC continues to accept applications and submissions via existing channels.
Parallel run period extension and upcoming enhancements
Since its implementation, the SFC has closely monitored the functioning of e-IP and actively engaged with industry participants to obtain their feedback on user experience.

While e-IP has garnered widespread industry support and is running smoothly, new features and more advanced settings will be introduced to further enhance user experience based on users’ comments. To facilitate these enhancements, the SFC will extend the parallel run period of e-IP by one month to 29 November 2024.
Full adoption of e-IP

Starting 30 November 2024, ie, after the parallel run period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by IPD must be submitted via e-IP. The current submission requests from IPD via the IP E-submission system will be integrated into e-IP, including reporting of net asset values, large redemptions and suspensions of dealing. In addition, e-IP users can also settle recurring annual fees associated with relevant investment products through the new system.
Feedback and enquiries
The SFC will continue to review and enhance the operation of e-IP where practicable. If you have any questions, please contact the relevant case officers.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission
End

1 Investment-linked assurance schemes, mandatory provident fund products, open-ended fund companies, paper gold schemes, pooled retirement funds, real estate investment trusts, unit trusts and mutual funds and unlisted structured investment products.
2 Web-based INteGrated Service.

candidate.controlled_language: Selected control: compulsory e-IP submission route from 30 November 2024. For each covered application or submission made from that date, submission to IPD must use e-IP. The extended parallel run permits existing channels through 29 November 2024. Enhancement plans do not make the transition conditional, and the annual-fee facility remains optional. The formal result tests only routing when its scope holds; an out-of-scope item receives no compliance verdict from this control.
candidate.revision_reason: The express text supports one mandatory-route reading, without a sufficiently grounded rival that postpones the date, exempts existing cases or makes annual-fee payment compulsory. A covered submission made through an existing non-e-IP channel on 29 November 2024 falls within the extended parallel run; the same submission on 30 November falls within the compulsory e-IP control and fails that route check. A fee payment alone does not become a covered submission merely because e-IP can process it. The strongest uncertainty concerns operational treatment of legacy-case follow-ups and the event fixing the submission date.

candidate.controlled_language: From 30 November 2024, an actor making an application or submission to IPD concerning any investment product administered by IPD must use e-IP. Footnote 1 describes the relevant product remit without imposing a separate list-membership condition. Integrated reporting requests illustrate covered submission functions but do not establish reporting deadlines. Fee settlement remains optional, and enhancement practicability does not qualify the route requirement. A true result within scope satisfies only this selected route control.
candidate.revision_reason: Gives controlling effect to the repeated functional phrase 'administered by IPD'; footnote membership is descriptive rather than an additional condition. It differs from r1 only if IPD administers a product outside the listed classes. The strongest uncertainty is whether the footnote was intended as a complete definition. Hypotheses restricting the duty to existing e-IP users or conditioning commencement on practicable enhancements fail: the user reference concerns optional fees, and practicability concerns SFC enhancements. The supplied incomparable-pair diagnostics do not resolve any of these questions.

candidate.controlled_language: Selected control: compulsory e-IP submission route from 30 November 2024. Each covered application or submission made from that date must use e-IP. Existing channels remain accepted during the extended parallel run through 29 November 2024. Enhancement plans do not expressly condition that transition, and annual-fee settlement through e-IP remains optional. candidate.revision_reason: Retain the parent's mandatory-route reading with explicit evidentiary limits. A covered submission using an existing non-e-IP channel on 29 November is outside this mandatory control and within the extended acceptance period; the same item submitted on 30 November fails the route check. A fee payment alone does not establish coverage. Hypotheses that enhancements postpone the deadline, 'where practicable' excuses submitters, the full-adoption heading makes fee payment compulsory, or case initiation before transition creates grandfathering lack textual support. The uncited units add context and attribution, not a justified rival rule. The five INCOMPARABLE_FACT_BINDINGS diagnostics supply no substantive counterexample and therefore justify no change to fact meanings. The strongest remaining uncertainty is the classification and timing of legacy-case follow-ups.

units.text: This circular informs the industry that the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) will extend the parallel run period of its new online application/submission system for investment products, e-IP, by one month to 29 November 2024. After the extended period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by the Investment Products Division (IPD)1 must be submitted to IPD via e-IP from 30 November 2024.
Background

Following the “Circular on launch of e-IP application/submission system on WINGS” dated 8 July 2024, the SFC launched e-IP on its WINGS2 portal on 29 July 2024 to streamline and enhance the efficiency of processing new product applications and post-authorisation/registration submissions to IPD.

A three-month period of parallel run from the launch of e-IP up to 29 October 2024 was provided at the initial stage. During this period, the SFC continues to accept applications and submissions via existing channels.
Parallel run period extension and upcoming enhancements
Since its implementation, the SFC has closely monitored the functioning of e-IP and actively engaged with industry participants to obtain their feedback on user experience.

While e-IP has garnered widespread industry support and is running smoothly, new features and more advanced settings will be introduced to further enhance user experience based on users’ comments. To facilitate these enhancements, the SFC will extend the parallel run period of e-IP by one month to 29 November 2024.
Full adoption of e-IP

Starting 30 November 2024, ie, after the parallel run period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by IPD must be submitted via e-IP. The current submission requests from IPD via the IP E-submission system will be integrated into e-IP, including reporting of net asset values, large redemptions and suspensions of dealing. In addition, e-IP users can also settle recurring annual fees associated with relevant investment products through the new system.
Feedback and enquiries
The SFC will continue to review and enhance the operation of e-IP where practicable. If you have any questions, please contact the relevant case officers.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission
End

1 Investment-linked assurance schemes, mandatory provident fund products, open-ended fund companies, paper gold schemes, pooled retirement funds, real estate investment trusts, unit trusts and mutual funds and unlisted structured investment products.
2 Web-based INteGrated Service.

After the extended period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by the Investment Products Division (IPD)1 must be submitted to IPD via e-IP from 30 November 2024.
Background

Following the “Circular on launch of e-IP application/submission system on WINGS” dated 8 July 2024, the SFC launched e-IP on its WINGS2 portal on 29 July 2024 to streamline and enhance the efficiency of processing new product applications and post-authorisation/registration submissions to IPD.

A three-month period of parallel run from the launch of e-IP up to 29 October 2024 was provided at the initial stage. During this period, the SFC continues to accept applications and submissions via existing channels.
Parallel run period extension and upcoming enhancements
Since its implementation, the SFC has closely monitored the functioning of e-IP and actively engaged with industry participants to obtain their feedback on user experience.

While e-IP has garnered widespread industry support and is running smoothly, new features and more advanced settings will be introduced to further enhance user experience based on users’ comments. To facilitate these enhancements, the SFC will extend the parallel run period of e-IP by one month to 29 November 2024.
Full adoption of e-IP

Starting 30 November 2024, ie, after the parallel run period, applications and submissions of investment products administered by IPD must be submitted via e-IP. The current submission requests from IPD via the IP E-submission system will be integrated into e-IP, including reporting of net asset values, large redemptions and suspensions of dealing. In addition, e-IP users can also settle recurring annual fees associated with relevant investment products through the new system.
Feedback and enquiries
The SFC will continue to review and enhance the operation of e-IP where practicable. If you have any questions, please contact the relevant case officers.
Investment Products Division
Securities and Futures Commission
